summary.intent: Win the Lio 'Keep the Line Running' hackathon challenge for Soony by analyzing the confidential supply-chain data drop, then building a general, adaptable agent product that rechecks the launch plan, surfaces contradictions with sources, and takes real supplier actions.
summary.outcome: Analyzed the data and found that the Collector's Edition misses launch (overbooked art books, failed statues, sleeve revision conflict, Hwaseong offload) despite an 'ok' plan. Built a polling/versioned-store/LLM paper-check pipeline, routines automation backend and UI, a verifier shortfall fix (34,800 to 6,800 with a document reading), briefing docs/pages, interview prep, and a calm 'Today' UI redesign, with most work committed on jonas/alert-platform.

repo: Confidential portal data lives in gitignored data/ (raw, drops, notes, design, img); .env holds SOONY_PORTAL_TOKEN and .env.example is committed with an empty token.
Portal API has only three endpoints (files list, single file, archive.zip); no webhooks, so the product must poll and compare SHA-256 because existing files are replaced under the same name.
Team workflow is defined in CLAUDE.md and PROGRESS.md; tasks are claimed with a 'Now' line in PROGRESS.md, and work is on branch jonas/alert-platform (PR #5 open into main).
Entire hooks only write a checkpoint when repo files change; sessions with no repo changes log 'no files modified, skipping checkpoint'.

The paper check (papercheck.py) finds 9 cards deterministically even without a model; scripts/demo_cards.py is now a thin wrapper, and --reset should be run before the demo, with no ASK_BACKGROUND=on restart before it.
Verifier shortfall now tracks arriving and not_counted inbound; arrivals are counted only if a supplier shipping document has been read, otherwise the inbound is conservatively not counted.

Routines engine supports four triggers (decisions, waiting, shipments, replies), steps chase/call/ask_status, trust modes ask/tell/quiet, and undo with honest refusal reasons; proposals are stored in routine_proposals.json.
BOM double-counts the CE lid magnets, which PackRight fits into the box, so the magnet shortage is a false alarm.

code.finding: gap = needed - usable - arriving; an inbound counts only if its ETA is on or before launch, it is not cancelled or arrived at the port, it has no receipt already in stock, it is not overdue, and the shipping document does not say less.
The allocate card's evidence, question and approver message now use stock plus arriving, and the card disappears once the gap closes.
The wide routine flow was rewritten as When/Then/Always lanes that wrap, while the narrow vertical view is unchanged.
Documents the verifier changes and what is left: run-dry time ignores arrivals, and impact/__main__.py does not print the arriving list.

workflow: Subagents work well for parallel cross-checks (order confirmations and scans) and for builders with disjoint file ownership, such as backend, routines UI, designer and verifier.
Specific office-hours questions show the team has read the data, while general pain and product questions feed the business case; order questions by importance because of the lottery.
Confidential data should stay out of git and out of shared artifacts; artifacts are private by default and should only be shared with the team.
The design canvas needs files inside the project folder (data/design/project), and a calm, minimal one-decision-at-a-time design was preferred over cluttered dashboards.
Do not modify a teammate's module unilaterally unless they are unavailable; here the user approved fixing Farhan's verifier while Farhan was asleep, leaving a note.

friction: The portal token was initially empty, so the API returned 401 until it was filled in.
Entire's checkpoint skipping made it look like hooks had not fired.
Codex hooks still need approval in /hooks.
The first design canvas directions were rejected as far too cluttered, which meant a redesign and a rebuild of the front end.
Two cards contradicted each other (34,800 vs 6,800) because the verifier ignored deliveries before the end of packing.
The live dashboard still shows 34,800 on this Mac because Hwaseong's shipping advice has no local reading.
A Teams header emoji replacement missed a multi-line header and needed a manual fix.
Two obsolete tests and a dead fixture for the removed hand-written demo cards had to be cleaned up.
Artifact publishing initially failed because the canvas files had to sit inside the project folder.
ruff format flags two dispatch/decisions files that were already unformatted.
open_items: Run a paid OpenAI image-recognizer reading of Shipping_advice_020-48113256 so the dashboard shows 6,800, which needs the user's OK.
Push the ~20 local commits on jonas/alert-platform (PR #5 still open), pending the user's approval.
Register sender email addresses in portal Settings and set up a sending inbox, then send the Karton Nowak art book order (offer valid 24h) and reply to Boise about EXW terms.
Restyle the routine diagram calmly to match the Today look, and finish and verify the Today front-end rebuild before committing.
Fix the verifier's run-dry/act-by time to account for arrivals, and print the arriving list in impact/__main__.py (left for Farhan).
Decide whether to delete the earlier Claude doc, update the briefing page with the 14:37 drop, and fix the PackRight routine offer that is misplaced on the Boise decision screen.
Answer whether portal data is identical across teams and whether supplier replies create portal files by asking the Lio engineers.

Statue concession and Collector's Items Category Lead vacancy, the sleeve revision B vs C question, and the 78,000 unexplained pre-order pins remain unresolved business questions.
